answer: Staked collateral resists sybil attacks by pricing every identity at its true cost of forgery. Agent shippers that haul saffron between two harbors must each deposit a bond before they can bid; an operator running a hundred fake shippers must fund a hundred bonds, and any account detected sharing one controller is slashed. One bad season, a gale that delays every honest ship, changes nothing because the attacker's exposure stays a hundred times the trader's. Agents therefore keep the protocol as their haven: cloning is cheap only until it must actually pay.
